_PLANTED_ARTIFACTS: OPTIONAL, per domain block. If your lab or UAT environment contains a DELIBERATELY planted secret, credential-shaped string, or other artifact that an honest harvest will find and cannot explain, DECLARE IT. Put a `_plantedArtifacts` string on the domain block that owns it, naming the exact field and saying it is synthetic, why it is there, and that it must still never be restated or propagated. WHY: a domain protocol may require the leg to HALT on out-of-scope drift - an unexplained credential in the resource it is about to change is exactly that, and the rule exists because silently absorbing it could launder an out-of-band production change through the gate. An undeclared plant therefore blocks your run every time, correctly, and you cannot fix it by weakening the rule without removing the control that makes the run worth anything. Declaring it converts UNEXPLAINED into KNOWN and leaves the rule armed for everything else. Scope the declaration to the named artifacts and say so - any other credential-shaped value is still undeclared drift. Live 2026-09-19: an AWS access-key pattern in a resource TAG (which the provider's own `sensitive_attributes` redaction does not cover, because it protects attributes and not tags) was found by the harvester, correctly not restated, and correctly blocked at the gate for want of a human triage that nobody had pre-supplied.
_ALLOCATIONS: OPTIONAL, per domain block, and the ONLY place an allocation fact can live. An allocation is a statement about what was RESERVED for a purpose - a parent range for a pool, an address block for a tenant, an ASN range. No harvest can produce one: a device carries what is CONFIGURED on it and has no representation of what was set aside. If a requirement asks a leg to establish such a boundary from harvest evidence, that requirement is unsatisfiable and the leg will either escalate (correct) or infer one from the shape of whatever happens to be configured (plausible and wrong). Put the fact here as `<domain>._allocations`, or - just as important - declare that NONE exists, because an absent allocation and an undeclared one are indistinguishable from a leg's seat. Live 2026-09-19: three rounds inferred a /24 parent range from six addresses sharing their top 24 bits; a fourth refused and escalated, and the obligation was retired. Where no allocation exists, minimality - the derived range covers exactly the harvested set and nothing else - is the control that remains.

_note: A domain-specific block. Rename/replace for your domain. What makes it a GOOD block is the
pattern below, not the field names: state the STATIC constraints as values, and state each
RUNTIME-DERIVED value explicitly as runtime — with a `_why` field saying why it cannot be
known up front. A value left ambiguous is a value an agent will guess.
_domainBlock_EXAMPLE_telemetryExport.exporterPool: {{static constraint — a value that IS knowable up front}}
_domainBlock_EXAMPLE_telemetryExport.existingAllocations: RUNTIME — discoverable only by harvesting the live devices
_domainBlock_EXAMPLE_telemetryExport.selectedExporterAddresses: RUNTIME — selected by the design leg from live state
_domainBlock_EXAMPLE_telemetryExport.derivedExporterAggregate: RUNTIME — derived by the design leg; chained downstream
_domainBlock_EXAMPLE_telemetryExport._whyThisIsUnarguablyRuntime: {{The objective test. Strongest form: the value changes on every environment rebuild, so it cannot be pinned in a static artifact or agreed in an interface contract, and the Program Architect structurally cannot know it.}}

_note: KEEP THIS BLOCK for any multi-pipeline program. It is the machine-readable counterpart to
requirements.md's 'Why this is sequenced' section, and the two must agree.
THE TEST that decides the value of `kind`:
Is every value the downstream domain needs knowable BEFORE the upstream domain runs?
yes -> 'parallel'   ... the values belong in the INTERFACE CONTRACT
no  -> 'sequenced'  ... the value must ride a DAG EDGE (inter-pipeline chaining)
Getting this wrong in the parallel direction is the expensive one: the downstream leg starts
with a value nobody could have known, and either guesses or stalls.
interdependency.chainedValue: {{the value that crosses the edge, or null if parallel}}
interdependency.direction_note: {{which leg produces, which consumes, and what the consumer must NOT do — e.g. 'the consumer re-states the chained value and is forbidden from recomputing it'}}
